rule_description: Extract CPU-only tests — move CPU-only tests into the original-named class with @instantiate_parametrized_tests or plain TestCase

action_items.description: Helper _compute_tolerances (lines 481-485) calls torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0) to loosen tolerances on CUDA SM86. The catalog lists get_device_capability under category_a.same_name (replaceable) but ALSO under category_c.cuda.device_properties, and the return type differs per backend (tuple[int,int] on CUDA/MTIA vs dict[str,Any] on accelerator/XPU), so a naive torch.accelerator.get_device_capability replacement would break the `== (8, 6)` comparison.
action_items.recommendation: Make _compute_tolerances device-agnostic: guard the SM86 branch with a device_type=='cuda' check before comparing the capability tuple (device-type-aware comparison). The 5 calling tests (test_cnn_model_sum, test_cnn_model_mean, test_instance_norm_model, test_group_norm_model, test_layer_norm_model) stay device-agnostic - the tolerance tweak is a precision nicety, not the subject of the tests.

action_items.description: test_expanded_weight_forward contains an in-body device conditional `if "cuda" in device and "max_norm" in sample_input.kwargs and "padding_idx" in sample_input.kwargs: self.skipTest(...)` for non-deterministic CUDA embedding (issue #74679). Per the classification guide, a device conditional in the test body does NOT make a test device_specific.
action_items.recommendation: Keep as-is (device-agnostic). The embedding skip is also mirrored by a DecorateInfo in common_methods_invocations.py (line 21822), so leave the in-body skip untouched.

action_items.description: Legacy module-level nn-tests harness (lines 1022-1055) dynamically attaches CPU and CUDA-named tests (<name>, <name>_multiple_inputs, <name>_cuda_double) to TestExpandedWeightModule via setattr, hardcoding the device strings 'cpu'/'cuda' and gating the CUDA variants on TEST_CUDA. The comment at line 1017 says these should become ModuleInfo tests. This is the ONLY consumer of the TEST_CUDA import and the source of hardcoded 'cuda' test names.
action_items.recommendation: Out of scope for the CPU-only/device-agnostic/device-specific strategy conversion (the dynamic tests are not static `def test_` methods), but flag for follow-up: modernizing this harness to ModuleInfo-based tests would remove the hardcoded device strings, the CUDA-named variants, and the TEST_CUDA dependency. Keep the loop and the TEST_CUDA import for now.

action_items.description: tf32_off() decorator from common_cuda is applied to 6 device-agnostic tests (test_cnn_model_sum, test_cnn_model_mean, test_instance_norm_model, test_group_norm_model, test_layer_norm_model, test_module) as a CUDA TF32 precision control. It is a test decorator, not a Category C API call in the test bodies, so it does NOT make these tests device-specific and does not require keeping @onlyCUDA (none exists).
action_items.recommendation: Retain the tf32_off import and all 6 @tf32_off() decorators unchanged. Do not flag these tests as Category C.

action_items.description: External reference: TestExpandedWeightFunctional is referenced by a DecorateInfo entry in torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py (line 21822) that skips test_expanded_weight_forward for the nn.functional.embedding OpInfo. DecorateInfo matches against the generic class name, so any rename of TestExpandedWeightFunctional would break this skip unless the DecorateInfo is updated.
action_items.recommendation: Keep the original class names for all classes (no renaming). Renaming is optional per the workflow, and here it would create external-reference churn in common_methods_invocations.py with no benefit since the file is already uniformly device-agnostic.
